basic_info.name: FIGMA (FIne-Grained Music retrievAl) — multi-view contrastive music retrieval model; companion dataset FGMCaps
basic_info.org: Nishit Anand, Ashish Seth, Sreyan Ghosh, Dinesh Manocha, Ramani Duraiswami — University of Maryland (UMD)
basic_info.release_date: arXiv 2606.06615 (June 2026); ACL 2026 (San Diego, July 2026), main conference long paper
basic_info.links: paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06615 ; ACL Anthology: https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.2197/ ; project page: https://nishitanand.github.io/figma-website/ ; code (inference): https://github.com/nishitanand/FIGMA ; model: https://huggingface.co/nishitanand/FIGMA ; FGMCaps train data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/nishitanand/FGMCaps-data ; FGMCaps benchmark: https://huggingface.co/datasets/nishitanand/FGMCaps-benchmark

architecture.backbone: Frozen pretrained encoders with only lightweight projection heads trained (~22M trainable params; frozen encoders total ~800M): MuQ audio encoder (self-supervised music model, frame features B x 250 x 1024) + Microsoft Multilingual E5 Large Instruct text encoder (token features B x 128 x 1024). Each projector = 2 Transformer encoder layers (8 heads, FF dim 512) + linear projection to shared 512-d space
architecture.input_modality: audio (10-second music clips at 24 kHz) + text captions (English; E5 is multilingual but training data is English)
architecture.training_objective: Multi-View Contrastive loss: (1) global InfoNCE on mean-pooled audio vs [CLS] text embeddings, (2) frame-level token-wise InfoNCE — for each audio frame, take max similarity to any text token, average per-frame scores, batch-negative InfoNCE (chosen over SIGLIP-style BCE for stability); combined with weight alpha=0.6 global / 0.4 frame. Trained 15 epochs, batch 256, Adam lr 1e-4, temperature 0.07, early stopping on R@1
architecture.embedding_output: 512-dim shared embedding space; BOTH global (mean-pooled audio / CLS text) and frame-level (250 audio frames x 512, aligned token-wise with 128 text tokens) embeddings produced by the same projectors; L2-normalized for cosine similarity

data.training_data: FGMCaps: 380K music-caption pairs for training + 10K test set: first large-scale dataset combining music-theoretic annotations (chord progression, tempo, beat count, key/mode) with natural-language captions plus genre/mood metadata. Audio from 4 public sources: MTG-Jamendo, Music4All, JamendoMaxCaps, MusicBench. Attributes auto-extracted: BeatNet (tempo/beat), Omnizart (chords), Essentia KeyExtractor (key); captions generated by Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct from structured attribute prompts with randomized attribute order. Bench set includes FGMCaps-Eval (1,000 out-of-domain pairs from Free Music Archive). Dataset licenses per source not verified [uncertain]

performance.benchmarks: Embedding-family, text-music retrieval benchmark (R@1/5/10/20, T2A + A2T): MusicBench T2A R@1 34.52 / R@5 65.99 / R@10 81.73 / R@20 91.37 (vs CLaMP 3: 28.3 / 57.87 / 74.62 / 89.5; vs M2D-CLAP lower at R@1 30.7 [uncertain — partial table only]); out-of-domain FGMCaps-Eval (FMA): +73.3% relative over best baseline; in-domain FGMCaps test: T2A R@1 26.15 vs best baseline 2.22. Hard-negative attribute-perturbation probe (3K clips, perturbing key/BPM/tempo-marking/chord one at a time): maintains 34-43% A2T R@1. Not evaluated on MuChoMusic or Song Describer
performance.vs_clap: Outperforms 10+ baselines incl. all LAION-CLAP variants, MS-CLAP 2022, M2D-CLAP, CLaMP 3, MuQ-MuLaN; +21.4% relative over previous best (CLaMP 3) on MusicBench T2A R@1; up to +73.3% relative out-of-domain. Key finding: LAION-CLAP uses only first ~50 caption tokens (truncating MusicBench captions to 50 tokens gives ~identical retrieval), and fine-tuning LAION-CLAP on FGMCaps itself gives only marginal gains — bottleneck is the objective, not data

availability.license: Inference code MIT; model checkpoint CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial, because it bundles MuQ encoder weights which are CC BY-NC 4.0; E5 is MIT); FGMCaps data/benchmark licenses follow source datasets, not verified [uncertain]

fit_for_local_playlist.sample_rate: 24 kHz mono input (MuQ convention) — needs resampling from repo-standard 48 kHz mono
fit_for_local_playlist.inference_cost: ~800M params forward per track (frozen MuQ 10 s clip + E5), 22M trainable but all params execute at inference; trained batch 256 on GPUs — per-track latency not published [uncertain]; CPU feasible but slow [uncertain]
fit_for_local_playlist.full_track_context: 10 s clip input only (T=250 frames); full tracks require windowed inference + aggregation (aggregation scheme for whole-track embedding not specified in paper) [uncertain]
fit_for_local_playlist.frame_level_support: Yes — natively produces 250 frame-level x 512-d audio embeddings aligned token-wise to text; frame-level alignment is explicitly usable at inference (GFMCaps-style queries ground tempo->rhythm frames, key->harmony frames). Best frame-level architecture in this study
fit_for_local_playlist.multilingual_queries: Text encoder is multilingual E5-Large-Instruct, but training captions are English; non-English query behavior not evaluated [uncertain]
fit_for_local_playlist.retrieval_steering: Strong attribute control for tempo/key/chord/beat via plain-text attribute-rich queries (its core contribution); no separate steering API, and no attribute-conditioned audio-audio retrieval mode
